groups.sentence: Instructors teach, remind and discuss with students that AI output can be wrong and must be verified.
Students verify the accuracy of AI-generated content before using or submitting it.
Everyone reviews and verifies AI output for accuracy before using, sharing or relying on it.
Students check that sources and references cited by AI exist and are accurate.
Instructors and staff review and verify the accuracy of AI output they use or produce.
Students treat AI output as a draft or starting point and assume it is wrong unless verified.
Students must not rely on, cite or accept AI output or sources without verifying them.
Instructors ask students to evaluate or verify AI output as part of assignments.
Everyone should not treat AI output as automatically accurate or rely on it without critical scrutiny.
Everyone tests and verifies AI-generated code before using it.
Students document the steps they took to verify AI output.
AI output can be inaccurate, fabricated or biased, including fake citations.
Students should be aware that AI can be wrong, biased or make things up.
